posts.title: The Man Beethoven Trusted — and History Forgot
posts.description: I recently read Beyond The Art of Finger Dexterity: Reassessing Carl Czerny, edited by David Gramit (Cambridge University Press), one of the few recent academic books devoted entirely to Czerny. And I must say: it helped me understand Carl Czerny more than I could have imagined. Or, to put it differently: it opened a perspective that was quite shocking. posts.title: Brahms' Final Piece Sounds Like a Dying Heartbeat
posts.description: A reflection on Johannes Brahms’s late organ chorale prelude Herzlich thut mich verlangen, Clara Schumann, and the musical image of a fading heartbeat.

posts.title: Did Franz Liszt Really Understand Chopin’s Music?
posts.description: Arthur Friedheim’s 1916 edition of Chopin’s Études raises difficult questions about Franz Liszt, Chopin tradition, metronome marks, Karl Mikuli, Anton Rubinstein, and Whole Beat Metronome Practice.
